intro: One plate of mee hailam is roughly 550 kcal. Most of the calories come from the yellow mee and the thick gravy made with flour, soy sauce and oil.

variants.name: Fried mee hailam (less gravy, more oil)

diet: Yes, and it has decent protein from the chicken, prawns or squid. Calories are moderately high because the thick gravy has oil and flour. As a lunch with plain water, it can still fit. Watch the portion and skip extra fried sides.
tips: Ask for extra seafood or chicken to boost protein.
Add more sawi and leave some of the gravy.
Choose bihun hailam if you want a slightly lighter version.

swap.name: Bihun sup
swap.why: Clear soup with no flour or oil, so almost half the calories.

faq.q: Why is it called mee hailam?
faq.a: The name is linked to the Hainanese community, known for this style of cooking. In Malaysia, it's a common dish at tomyam shops and restaurants.

faq.q: What's the difference between mee hailam and mee goreng?
faq.a: Mee hailam usually has a thick, dark gravy. Mee goreng is stir-fried dry.

faq.q: Why is mee hailam gravy so thick?
faq.a: It's thickened with cornflour and egg, and flavoured with dark soy sauce and oyster sauce.
